intended_object: The standard bijection between multiplicative characters R → R' (monoid homs that send non-units to 0) and group homomorphisms Rˣ → R'ˣ. Its inverse extends a unit-group hom by zero. I took this from the docstring and the module documentation ("restriction / extension by zero gives an equivalence").
explanation:
The forward map is `toUnitHom`, which is `Units.map χ`, so it restricts χ to the unit groups. The inverse is `ofUnitHom f`, which sends x to f(x) when x is a unit and to 0 otherwise. Because a `MulChar` is 0 on every non-unit, it is determined by its values on units (the `ext` lemma). So the two maps are mutually inverse, and the proofs in the definition show exactly this.

The setting is a commutative monoid R and a commutative monoid with zero R'. This is the generality in which `MulChar` itself is defined, and a zero in the target is needed so that non-units have somewhere to go. The construction uses no further hypotheses.

Degenerate cases also work. When R' is trivial (0 = 1), both sides have exactly one element.

I found no other Mathlib declaration of this equivalence, so there is no counterpart to cite.
